atlas-gb.0268: Apply only after the university has told the Home Office you finished: an early application is refused and the fee is lost.
atlas-gb.0270: For a degree from the last five years at a university on the Home Office’s Global Universities List (TUM, PSL, TU Delft, KU Leuven, ETH Zurich among them; specialist business schools are not): two years, any work, capped at 8,000 a year, English at B2.
atlas-gb.0273: A licensed sponsor assigns a Certificate of Sponsorship for a graduate-level job (RQF 6); English at B2 since 8 January 2026. There is no general visa for jobs below degree level.
atlas-gb.0274: The lower new-entrant rate applies to under-26s and to people switching from Student or Graduate, for four years in total including Graduate time.
atlas-gb.0275: £41,700, or the occupation’s going rate if higher
atlas-gb.0277: £33,400, or 70% of the going rate if higher
atlas-gb.0279: £819 from abroad, £943 in the UK + health surcharge £1,035 a year
atlas-gb.0280: Settlement comes after five years on this visa; time on Student or Graduate visas does not count.
atlas-gb.0281: PhD, Global Talent and research routes
atlas-gb.0282: A PhD is a Student visa that keeps the right to bring family; STEM candidates outside the EU, US, Canada, Australia and Japan need ATAS clearance.
atlas-gb.0283: Researchers come on Global Talent after endorsement by UKRI, the Royal Society or the British Academy, which leads to settlement in three years, or on Skilled Worker.
atlas-gb.0287: There is no youth-mobility deal with the EU or the US. An EU–UK scheme is under negotiation but not agreed.
atlas-gb.0288: For citizens of Australia, Canada, New Zealand and South Korea aged 18 to 35, and of Andorra, Iceland, Japan, Monaco, San Marino and Uruguay aged 18 to 30; Taiwan, Hong Kong and India by ballot. Two years of any work, three for Australians, Canadians and New Zealanders.
atlas-gb.0291: EU and US citizens need an Electronic Travel Authorisation, valid two years; visa nationals need a Standard Visitor visa. Up to six months for tourism, meetings, interviews, short courses or thesis research, with no work.
atlas-gb.0292: Irish citizens need nothing: under the Common Travel Area they live and work in the UK freely.
atlas-gb.0294: A visitor cannot switch to a student or work visa inside the UK: you must apply from abroad.
atlas-gb.0295: Pay the Immigration Health Surcharge with your visa application: £1,035 a year, or £776 for students. It gives you NHS cover for the whole visa.
atlas-gb.0296: Never pay for a Certificate of Sponsorship or a “guaranteed visa”: the employer assigns and pays for the certificate, and job offers that ask you for visa fees up front are a known fraud.
atlas-gb.0297: Landlords must check your right to rent: give them a share code from gov.uk/prove-right-to-rent.
atlas-gb.0298: There is no physical card: residence permit cards (BRPs) have ended, and your status is an eVisa in your UKVI account, linked to your passport.
atlas-gb.0299: Apply online for a National Insurance number after you arrive. You may start work before it comes, by giving your employer a right-to-work share code; payroll uses an emergency tax code meanwhile.
atlas-gb.0300: The surcharge gives NHS cover but no family doctor: find a surgery at nhs.uk, register with form GMS1 and get your NHS number, needed for appointments and prescriptions.
atlas-gb.0301: Your eVisa is your digital proof of status: generate share codes, valid 90 days, at gov.uk/prove-right-to-work for employers, and keep your passport number up to date in your UKVI account before any trip, or you may be stopped at boarding.
atlas-gb.0302: Apply to extend or switch before your visa expires: your leave and its rights then continue by law until the decision (section 3C).
atlas-gb.0303: Do not leave the UK and Ireland while an application is pending: it is treated as withdrawn the day you leave, the fee is lost, and routes you can only apply for from inside, like the Graduate visa, are gone.
atlas-gb.0304: The Home Office never calls, texts or emails to ask for money or passport details; check your status only in your UKVI account.
atlas-gb.0305: Leave the UK and Common Travel Area while an extension or switch is pending and the application counts as withdrawn; if your old visa has expired you cannot come back.
atlas-gb.0306: Working as a visitor or on an ETA is a criminal offence, with removal and a re-entry ban.
atlas-gb.0307: Nobody can sell you a Certificate of Sponsorship: the employer pays for it. The Home Office never asks for money or passport details by phone or email.
atlas-gb.0308: There are no plastic residence cards any more: status is an eVisa, shown to employers and landlords with a share code.
atlas-gb.0309: Student funds rise to £1,570 a month in London and £1,203 elsewhere for applications from 30 November 2026.
atlas-gb.0310: An EU–UK youth experience scheme for 18 to 30 year olds is being negotiated, with no date.
atlas-gb.0311: The government consulted on “earned settlement”, raising the usual wait for settlement to ten years.
atlas-gb.0312: A new Global Universities List for the HPI visa is due in November 2026.
atlas-gb.0313: A £925 yearly levy per international student on English universities from 2028 may feed into tuition fees.
